chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from one who heard him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And the Jews said: The Hand of Allah is chained», they did not mean that it is literally so, but rather they said: The matter has been completed, so He does not add nor subtract.
So Allah, Glorified be His Glory, said in denial of their saying: «Chained be their hands! And they were cursed for what they said. Rather, His Hands are extended; He spends how He wishes.»
Have you not heard Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, say: «Allah erases what He wishes, and He confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book».

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz)

ai.seo_question: What did the Jews mean by saying 'The Hand of Allah is chained' and how did Allah refute it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Jewish assertion of a 'chained' divine hand was a theological claim of fatalism, suggesting that God's decree was finalized and immutable. He refutes this by citing the extended hands of Allah, linking it to the concept of *al-Mahw wa al-Ithbat* (erasure and confirmation) found in Surah Ar-Ra'd, which affirms that divine decree is dynamic and subject to God's will rather than rigidly fixed.
